spans.text: The crypto market went through a sharp correction this week, with Bitcoin briefly losing the
support level and dropping more than 7% in 24 hours. One of the symbolic triggers was the decision by Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy), led by Michael Saylor, to sell 32 BTC — roughly
$2.5 million

— to fund dividend payments. Although it's the company's first sale in years and represents only a tiny fraction of its 843,706 BTC treasury, the move dented investor sentiment, which had grown accustomed to the company's aggressive accumulation strategy.

With the market already heavily exposed, the sale was enough to set off a leverage "bomb." On-chain data shows the leverage ratio was at dangerous levels, comparable to those seen before the October 2025 crash. The result was a liquidation wave that hit
$1.85 billion
in positions over 24 hours, dragging the price down to a four-month low. Nearly 280,000 traders were liquidated, with most of the losses (around
$1.7 billion
) coming from long positions that were forced to close.
The capital flight: ETFs and the AI boom

The structural decline can't be explained by short-term dynamics alone. There's a deeper move of capital fleeing crypto for other assets. While Bitcoin struggles to regain momentum, the U.S. stock market — especially the AI sector — keeps setting new all-time highs. The Nasdaq 100 is up about 20% this year, and AI-related stocks have soared, creating a high opportunity cost for anyone holding Bitcoin.
Institutional flows reflect this shift in preference. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs posted net outflows of roughly
$4 billion

between May 15 and June 2. BTC exchange-traded products accumulated net outflows of 62,794 BTC over the past three weeks, marking the longest withdrawal streak since these funds launched. Instead of running to Bitcoin as a safe-haven asset, investors are raising capital to allocate into AI stocks and initial public offerings from companies like Anthropic and SpaceX.
